targetAudience.primary: Architects building resumable agents, durable sessions and recovery control planes
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands checkpoints, durable appends, retries and model-call lifecycles.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A failed acknowledgement leaves the runtime unable to tell whether a Session append committed, so blind retry can duplicate history and blind skip can lose it.

whyNow: A same-day merged OpenAI Agents Python change persists pending Session writes and reconciles them against authoritative history before resumed model execution.

externalHook.description: A checkpoint can restart execution without proving whether the preceding durable effect committed.

coreProposition: Uncertain persistence is a first-class recovery state that must suspend continuation authority: persist the unresolved intent, reread authoritative history, classify committed, absent or ambiguous state, and fail closed on ambiguity before any new model execution.

originalValue.description: Separates process resumability from durable-state certainty and frames reconciliation as evidence required for permission to continue.

readerTakeaway: Store pending durable intent in the checkpoint, reconcile it before new reasoning, and add a distinct ownership primitive when multiple restored workers can race.

supported: Pending Session-write identity and fingerprints are persisted in RunState.
Streaming and non-streaming resume paths reconcile before the next model call.
Exact history comparison distinguishes committed, unchanged and ambiguous outcomes.
unsupported: Transactional rollback of external tool effects
uncertain: How legitimate concurrent history extension should be merged
Whether future Session backends should expose revision or CAS tokens

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general resumable-runtime recovery pattern without a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged implementation supports a precise pre-model reconciliation rule and explicitly exposes the distributed limit.
